title: Migrating a legacy feature toggle to OpenFeature
answers: How do I migrate a feature toggle to OpenFeature?
How to move a feature flag off config.featureToggles?
Why does this flag have both LegacyFrontend and React generate options?
body: To migrate a toggle from legacy config to OpenFeature: in pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go set `Generate: Generate{LegacyFrontend: true, React: true}` on the flag entry (keep LegacyFrontend true if the flag key uses the old naming convention without a namespace, e.g. `perPanelNonApplicableDrilldowns` instead of `dashboard.perPanelNonApplicableDrilldowns`). Regenerate openfeature.gen.ts/openfeature-types.gen.d.ts to get a `useFlagX` hook and FlagKeys entry. In component code, replace `config.featureToggles.X` with either the generated `useFlagX()` hook (in React render code) or `getFeatureFlagClient().getBooleanValue(FlagKeys.X, false)` (outside render, e.g. in activate()/lifecycle methods). Once migrated, remove the file's entry from eslint-suppressions.json for the `@grafana/no-config-feature-toggles` rule since direct config.featureToggles access is no longer needed there.
applies: Any PR migrating a Grafana feature toggle from legacy config.featureToggles to OpenFeature.
